tast-tests: Add hardware.Memtester{Fast,Slow}. Port the hardware_Memtester.quick Autotest test to Tast as a new hardware.MemtesterFast local test. It just runs the external memtester command to test 10 MiB of memory. Also add a slower disabled hardware.MemtesterSlow test that matches the standard hardware_Memtester Autotest test. This change also introduces a new "hardware" test category. The existing "platform" category doesn't seem like a great fit for these tests, since "platform" primarily tests userspace functionality. We may want to consider moving the existing platform.TPMResponsive test to the hardware category. BUG=chromium:949744 TEST=manual: ran both tests against a caroline device Change-Id: Ib30200b3c34b69f7fe5de2c170e40d7a6f836800 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1553723 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Puthikorn Voravootivat <puthik@chromium.org>

tast-tests: Fix empty PID file race in security.Minijail. 86517da5b2fc updated security.Minijail's pid-file.static subtest to loop until it successfully reads the PID file written by minijail0, but minijail0 doesn't atomically create the file, so it looks like the subtest is likely still failing due to performing the read before the contents have been written. Move the file-content check within the loop condition so we wait until we get the expected data. Also map /usr/bin into the chroot since it's needed for the "sleep" command to work. BUG=chromium:950504,chromium:949357 TEST=manual: test passes locally; also ensured that "sleep" works within the shell Change-Id: I2691108795ab8a9a3403c83e8d70749ee435d85e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1562028 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>

ish: solve timer reliability and time jumps b:129805553 demonstrates that the time jumps by 2^32 us twice during boot. This appears to have been caused by leftover interrupts that have not been cleared while the system was booting triggering T0. In addition, b:124890290 discusses that the LRE bit should not be set in HPET configuration, and the do-while loop introduced in CL:1457597 is no longer needed if the settling spin-lock is placed before arming the timer. This resolves that BRANCH=none BUG=b:124890290,b:12980553 TEST=timer appears to be working reliably for 24 hours on arcada, no time jumps Change-Id: Ib0c6b8c9c7e8fe2111a312b9c48061b296178c72 Signed-off-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1548505 Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Paul Fagerburg <pfagerburg@chromium.org>

tpm_manager: fix TPM 1.2 nvram implementation errors This CL fixed the following issues. 1. policy handle was not set correctly so that any NVRAM access that requires authorization (owner or custom password) didn't work. 2. defining an index with an empty auth value and the attribute WRITE_AUTHORIZATION was impossible. 3. couldn't read-lock and write-lock an index in a single request. Also, 1. reduced code redundancy in tpm_nvram_impl.cc 2. unified the type of nvram size to uint32_t, aliging with the proto def BUG=b:128952103 TEST=on chell, run tpm_manager_client take_ownership, then run tpm_manager_client with 1. various nvram sub-commands (define, read/write, lock, etc) 2. various attributes, including a. PERSISTENT_WRITE_LOCK b. BOOT_[READ,WRITE]_LOCK c. [READ,WRITE]_AUTHORIZATION d. OWNER_[READ,WRITE] 3. w/ and w/o bind_to_pcr0 and PCR0 extension 4. various auths, including a. owner password b. empty/non-empty custom password c. no auth Also, mutually test nvram implementations in tpm_manager and cryptohome (which is currently used by production) and make sure everything that cryptohome supports works.
